gaps: Editor-side export creation (POST that triggers a new render) was not exercised in browser-sniff to avoid consuming the user's plan quota. CLI can still list and download existing exports.
Delete / mutation endpoints (delete-recording, delete-clip, delete-export) were not captured. v0.2 if needed.
Webinar registration endpoints were not exercised.
Business API v3 endpoints exist but are unreachable from this CLI (Bearer-key only) — intentional scope choice for Pro-tier user.
patterns: Cookie-import auth (auth login --chrome) — same pattern reused for any HttpOnly-cookie-protected web app
CloudFront-signed-URL TTL refresh — pattern for any service whose downloads use short-lived signed asset URLs
Cross-source readiness join over local SQLite — pattern any service with multi-stage async pipelines benefits from

novel_features.name: Priority-fallback grab
novel_features.description: Get whichever exists for a recording in priority order: transcript first, then audio tracks, then HLS video — your stated goal as a single command.
novel_features.rationale: Combines three Riverside endpoints (transcriptions, take/assets, vod) behind a single decision tree; exits with code naming the tier reached. No competing tool offers priority fallback for Pro-tier recordings.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent has a recording session ID, this is the one-shot command that gets the most useful asset that exists without polling three separate endpoints first.

novel_features.name: Bulk studio export with resume
novel_features.description: Walk every project / take / asset in a studio (or date range) and download transcripts + per-participant audio + HLS manifests with a resume cursor on `.runstate/`. The killer workflow no Pro-tier tool offers.
novel_features.rationale: Iterates projects -> takes -> assets endpoints, persists progress so interruption never restarts the walk. Riverside's web app has no bulk-export UI for non-Business tiers.
novel_features.why_it_matters: For an agent backing up a creator's archive, this is the only way to get every asset out of Riverside without 6-12 manual clicks per take.

novel_features.name: Transcript format converter
novel_features.description: Convert Riverside's editableWithVoiceActivity JSON (speakers + voice-activity timestamps) to VTT, SRT, plain text, JSON, or speaker-grouped Markdown — formats Riverside's own UI doesn't expose.
novel_features.rationale: Pure local transform on cached transcription data; Riverside natively exposes only SRT/TXT through its UI download but the API payload contains richer voice-activity data we can reformat.
novel_features.example: riverside-fm-pp-cli transcripts convert bf487406-af40-4bb4-b7f9-a6b49047b55d --format vtt --out episode-12.vtt
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs a transcript in WebVTT for a web player or JSON for downstream NLP, this command converts the locally-cached transcript without re-hitting the API.

novel_features.name: Cross-studio readiness board
novel_features.description: List every take across all your synced studios that is fully ready: cloud backup done, transcription finished, no participant track still uploading.
novel_features.rationale: Local SQLite join across recordings, transcriptions, and participants — no single Riverside API call returns this view, and the web app surfaces it only per-recording.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents helping a producer with multiple shows need one call to see what's ready to cut — not 4 studios x N projects of manual clicking.

novel_features.name: Signed-URL refresh + prefetch
novel_features.description: Re-walks production media + clip-assets to refresh short-lived CloudFront signed URLs; --prefetch downloads every asset body before TTL expires.
novel_features.rationale: Riverside CloudFront URLs are time-limited; the web app silently regenerates them on each page load but offers no "refresh all" surface or bulk prefetch.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to archive a project's media assets, this command races the TTL clock instead of failing midway through a download chain.

novel_features.name: Transcript full-text search
novel_features.description: SQLite FTS5 over locally-cached transcription bodies; speaker filter joins the speakers array; output names the session, project, matched line, and timestamp.
novel_features.rationale: The only way to grep your own three-year Riverside catalog. No API endpoint searches transcripts; the web app shows transcripts only one take at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents finding a quote or moment in a creator's backlog use this instead of opening Riverside studios one by one.

novel_features.name: Wait-until-ready
novel_features.description: Block until a take's backup, transcription, and/or AI generation are done; --include selects which facets to wait on; --timeout caps the wait. Exits 0 on ready, 2 on timeout.
novel_features.rationale: Polls three separate Riverside endpoints with adaptive backoff; useful when an editor-side automation needs to fire only after upload + transcription + AI clips are all finished.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent pipeline depend on Riverside readiness without busy-loops or hardcoded sleeps.

novel_features.name: Magic Clips harvest
novel_features.description: Gates on AI-generation-status=ready, lists Magic Clip exports for a project, refreshes each clip's signed URL, optionally downloads MP4s.
novel_features.rationale: Chains three separate Riverside surfaces (AI status + exports list + per-clip URL refresh); the web app exposes them as separate tabs with no programmatic seam.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent automates social-clip distribution, this is the one command to pull every Magic Clip with fresh, downloadable URLs.

novel_features.name: Speaker talktime stats
novel_features.description: From the cached voice-activity timestamps, compute seconds spoken per speaker, % of total, longest monologue, and interrupt count.
novel_features.rationale: Riverside captures voice-activity timestamps but never surfaces them as metrics. Pure local computation post-sync; mechanical aggregation no other tool offers.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents grading interview pacing or producer-host balance use this to answer talktime questions without re-watching takes.

novel_features.name: Stale take detector
novel_features.description: Cross-studio query: which recordings have been stuck in uploading / processing / transcribing past N hours? Catches dropped guest-wifi uploads and abandoned takes.
novel_features.rationale: Local SQLite query against synced recording status; Riverside has no UI for cross-studio stuck-upload triage.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Production agents catching stuck takes before the host has moved on use this to triage what needs guest re-upload.

narrative.headline: The first programmatic way to download every transcript, audio track, and video from your own Riverside.com account — no Business plan or API key required.
narrative.value_prop: Riverside.com makes you click through Studio → Project → Take → Transcript for every download, and locks the official API behind a custom-priced Business plan. This CLI imports your logged-in browser cookies and reaches the same internal API the web app uses, giving you priority-fallback grab, bulk studio export with resume, transcript search over your whole archive, and Magic Clips harvest with CloudFront URL refresh — features Riverside has never shipped to Pro users.
narrative.auth_narrative: Riverside Pro / Live / Webinar tiers don't get an API key — but the web app you log into uses an internal API gated only by HttpOnly session cookies. Run `riverside-fm-pp-cli auth login --chrome` once: the CLI reads `riverside_auth_access`, `riverside_auth_refresh`, `sweetsesh`, and `cloudfront_signed_url` from your local Chrome profile and reuses them. The Business API at platform.riverside.fm is NOT used by this CLI — it requires a Bearer key that Pro plans cannot issue, and rejects cookies outright.

quickstart.comment: Import your Riverside session cookies from local Chrome (no password, no API key)
Pull projects, takes, recordings, transcripts into the local SQLite store
Priority-fallback download: transcript first, then audio, then video

troubleshoots.fix: Cookies expired — re-run `auth login --chrome` after reopening riverside.com in Chrome

troubleshoots.symptom: 403 on download URL after a successful list
troubleshoots.fix: CloudFront signed URL TTL expired — run `media refresh --project <id>` to fetch fresh signed URLs
Take is too short to transcribe or transcription is still processing — run `wait <session-id> --include transcript`

troubleshoots.symptom: Business API 401 "The Api Key is required"
troubleshoots.fix: This CLI uses the cookie-authed riverside.com surface, not the Business API. You don't need an API key. If you see this, you're hitting platform.riverside.fm by mistake — file a bug.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs to programmatically access a Riverside.com account on Pro / Live / Webinar tier (i.e., no Business API key available). It's the right choice for backing up a creator's archive, batch-downloading transcripts/audio/video by date range, full-text-searching a podcast catalog, harvesting Magic Clips when AI generation finishes, or waiting on a recording to be ready before firing downstream automation. It is NOT the right choice for write operations (creating studios, inviting guests, posting webhooks) — those surfaces exist in the API but weren't exercised in this print.
